newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish govt welcomes Enterprise Oil gas find.
newsitem.headline: Irish govt welcomes Enterprise Oil gas find.

text.p: Irish Minister of State for Transport and Energy Emmett Stagg said on Thursday it was too early draw to conclusions from a gas find by Enterprise Oil.

"The significance of the gas shows can only be determined when tests, to be completed by the end of October, have been run and the results of testing, together with all the other data from the well, have been fully evaluated," he said.

He was commenting on an announcement from Enterprise Oil Plc which said that its Corrib North Well in the Slyne Trough offshore the west of Ireland had reached total depth of 4370 metres and it was preparing to conduct a well-testing operation.

Stagg said in his statement that "it was too early to draw conclusions at this stage" but said he was confident the presence of gas would give an added incentive to further hydrcarbon exploration on the Irish western offshore.
He said it was also a timely boost for the Frontier Round in the Rockall for which applications have to be submitted by March 26 next year.
Enterprise Oil has a 45 percent stake and operates the well. Its partners are Santa Fe Exploration, which has a 40 percent interest and Statoil which owns 15 percent.
